## My path

My career has followed one question across two disciplines: how do
economic conditions shape human wellbeing and development?

I began as an economist. After earning my Candidate of Sciences
(Ph.D.) in Economics at the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine
with a dissertation on health and economic growth, I spent nearly a
decade as an Associate Professor of Finance & Econometrics at the
National University "Kyiv-Mohyla Academy" while working as a policy
researcher and analyst. In those years I co-authored Ukraine's
National Competitiveness Reports in partnership with the World
Economic Forum, contributed to the healthcare and education chapters
of Ukraine's National Program of Economic Reforms, and coordinated
analytical work with the World Bank, WHO, and international research
institutes.

That policy work kept returning me to a developmental insight:
economic circumstances matter most in childhood, when they shape the
trajectories that adult policy later struggles to correct. To study
those processes directly, I came to the University of Pittsburgh,
where I completed my Ph.D. in Developmental Psychology (with a minor
in Quantitative Methodology) in 2026, working with Dr. Elizabeth
Votruba-Drzal. My dissertation examined the long-term associations of
childhood family wealth — disaggregated into assets and debts — with
young adults' outcomes.
